newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Russia's Gazprom buys 34 pct of Bulgarian bank.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Gazprom buys 34 pct of Bulgarian bank.

text.p: Russia's gas giant Gazprom plans to acquire a 34-percent stake in the Bulgarian Credit Bank, part of the country's biggest private grouping Multigroup, its president said on Monday.
"Gazprom informed us of a decision of its board to subscribe 34 percent of the Credit Bank's capital, worth 10 billion levs," said Ilia Pavlov, who is also head of Credit Bank's board.
In July Credit Bank announced a capital rise to 10 billion levs from two billion levs through a new share issue worth eight billion levs.
Gazprom has had indirectly a stake in the Credit Bank through a Bulgarian gas firm Overgas Inc, in which the Russian company holds a 50-percent stake.
In July Overgaz subscribed five percent of Credit Bank's voting capital, which helped the firm's executive director Sasho Donchev to be elected to its board.

Under Bulgaria's banking regulations the central bank (BNB) should approve Gazprom's shares acquisition in Credit Bank. It is due to hold an exraordinary meeting within the next three months to approve Gazprom's representatives on the bank's board, Pavlov told a news conference.

Gazprom plans to invest some $600 million in the construction of gas pipelines in the Balkans, Pavlov said, adding that Credit Bank and Macedonia's Balkanska Banka would service Gazprom's activities in the region.
Credit Bank has some 30 percent in Balkanska Banka, which is based in Skopje.
Multigroup plans to invest another 60 million levs in Credit Bank, Pavlov said.
